          Stock grades (your watchlist)

          Grades the business (quality, health, growth) and the price (value), plus the chart trend. Click any row for the full plain-English report. These labels are research starting points, not buy/sell advice.

          How it works & words to know

          Your "thesis" (the why)
          One sentence on why you own a stock. You sell long-term stocks when that sentence stops being true, not when the price dips.
          Mr. Market
          Benjamin Graham's idea: the market is a moody partner offering prices every day. You don't have to accept them. Use his panic to buy, not to sell.
          Margin of safety
          Buy below what a business is worth, so even if you're somewhat wrong you don't lose much.
          Fair value (bear / base / bull)
          A rough range of what the business is worth if growth is slow / normal / fast. It's an estimate, not a promise.
          "Priced for perfection"
          The share price only makes sense if the company grows very fast for years. Any slip can drop the price a lot.
          Stop-loss / trailing stop
          For short-term trades only: a pre-decided price where you exit, so one bad trade can't become a big loss.
          Trim
          Sell part, keep part. Good for winners that got too big a share of your money.
          Quality
          Does it earn lots of profit on the money invested in it, with good margins and real cash?
          Health
          Low debt, enough cash, no dilution, business numbers not deteriorating.
          Growth
          Sales and profits rising year over year.
          Value
          Is the price reasonable for the profits and cash you get?
          Trend
          Is the share price itself rising? Useful for timing and short-term trades, not for judging the business.
          Graham's 7 tests
          The checklist from The Intelligent Investor for a cautious investor. Most modern tech stocks fail the price tests. That's normal; it tells you you're paying for growth.
          How often to look
          Run it daily or weekly. Act on SELL and REVIEW NOW. Glance at WATCH. Ignore the noise otherwise.
